safety_lead_time.comparison_action: Reduce SAP safety lead time from 3.0 to 2.0 days

narrative: Demand for PL1__MB70C9B5 is stable over the observed period (Mar 2025–Mar 2026) with a mean of 4,203 units/day and a coefficient of variation of 0.35, classifying it as a regular, near-normally distributed flow material. Nine outlier observations were winsorized to prevent bias in buffer calculations. Lead time variability (CV=0.215, std=1.13 days) is the dominant source of uncertainty, contributing 71.7% of total safety stock requirement. An (r,Q) continuous-review policy with EOQ-derived order quantity of 17,577 units and safety stock of 10,436 units is recommended, reducing the SAP safety stock by 2,987 units while maintaining 95% service level and delivering ~10% annual cost savings.
warnings: MOQ (2013) is non-binding: EOQ (17577) exceeds MOQ. Order quantity set to EOQ.
9 demand outliers detected and winsorized using IQR method before computing statistics.

research_insights.selected_model: (r,Q) Continuous-Review Reorder Point / Fixed Order Quantity (EOQ-based)
research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is stable with high frequency (98.4% non-zero days) and near-normal distribution. The (r,Q) policy minimises total ordering and holding costs via the EOQ formula while maintaining a statistically-derived safety stock for the 95% service level. It is the most appropriate model for high-frequency, predictable demand with moderate lead time variability.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity (240,295 units) is not a binding constraint. Safety stock (10,436) + EOQ (17,577) = 28,013 units, which is only 11.7% of maximum storage capacity. No capacity-driven policy reduction was required.
research_insights.escalation_flag: None. MOQ (2,013) is well below EOQ (17,577) and safety_stock + order_quantity is within storage limits. No infeasibility exists.
